title: School Dance Budget

events.description: You're in charge of the school dance budget — $50 total! You need decorations, snacks, and music. The DJ app costs $10, basic decorations are $15, and snacks for 30 people cost $20. That's $45 — leaving only $5 for extras. How do you allocate?

choices.label: DJ ($10) + Decor ($15) + Snacks ($20) + $5 buffer
choices.effect: A balanced plan with a small buffer! Smart to keep $5 for surprises.

choices.label: Better DJ ($20) + Basic decor ($10) + Snacks ($20)
choices.effect: Great music can make the dance! You spent it all but the vibe will be amazing.

choices.label: DJ ($10) + DIY decor ($5) + Snacks ($20) + $15 buffer
choices.effect: DIY decorations save money! You have $15 for unexpected needs. Resourceful!

events.description: Surprise! The snack prices went up by 15%. Your $20 snack budget now covers fewer items. What do you do?

choices.label: Use your buffer money for snacks
choices.effect: Good thing you planned ahead! The buffer covers the price increase.

choices.label: Buy fewer but better snacks
choices.effect: Quality over quantity! Fewer items but everyone loves them.

choices.label: Ask classmates to bring a snack each
choices.effect: Potluck style! Everyone contributes and you save money. Community solution!

events.description: A classmate suggests adding a photo booth. A DIY version costs $8, a fancy rental costs $25. Is it worth it?

choices.label: DIY photo booth ($8)
choices.effect: Props and a backdrop for $8! Everyone loves taking silly photos!

choices.label: Skip it — use phones instead
choices.effect: Phone cameras work great! You saved the money for other things.

choices.label: Quick fundraiser to cover it
choices.effect: You raised extra money with a quick bake sale! The booth is funded!

events.description: Dance night! Everything is set up. You have some money left over. What do you do with it?

choices.label: Save it for the next school event
choices.effect: Thinking ahead! The next event already has a head start on its budget.

choices.label: Buy thank-you treats for the helpers
choices.effect: What a thoughtful leader! Your team feels appreciated.

choices.label: Add a last-minute surprise for everyone
choices.effect: Glow sticks for everyone! A surprise hit at the dance!

recap_template: You managed a real event budget! You handled multiple categories, dealt with price changes, and made trade-offs. These are skills you'll use your whole life.
positive_framing_rules: Never say the student went over budget or messed up
Frame budget surprises as problem-solving opportunities

title: Comparison Shopper
learning_objectives: Calculate unit price for value comparison

events.description: Back-to-school shopping! You need a backpack, notebooks, and pens with $30. Store A has a backpack for $18, Store B has one for $22 but it's waterproof and has a warranty. What do you pick?

choices.label: Store A — $18 basic backpack
choices.effect: Good value! $12 left for the rest of your list.

choices.label: Store B — $22 waterproof with warranty
choices.effect: Might last longer and protect your stuff in rain! $8 left.

choices.label: Search online — $15 with free shipping (1 week wait)
choices.effect: Best price! But you'll have to wait a week. $15 left for other items.

events.description: Notebook time! A 3-pack costs $6, or you can buy singles for $2.50 each. You need 3 notebooks. Which is the better deal?

choices.label: 3-pack for $6 ($2.00 each)
choices.effect: The 3-pack saves you $1.50! Unit price comparison for the win!

choices.label: 3 singles for $7.50 ($2.50 each)
choices.effect: You got to pick 3 different colors! Sometimes variety is worth a little more.

choices.label: 2-pack ($4) + 1 fancy notebook ($4)
choices.effect: Two regular ones and one special one! A nice mix of value and quality.

events.description: Last item: pens! A 10-pack of basic pens is $3. A 5-pack of gel pens is $5. A single fancy pen is $4. What's the best value for you?

choices.label: 10 basic pens — $0.30 each
choices.effect: Best unit price! You'll have pens for months!

choices.label: 5 gel pens — $1.00 each
choices.effect: Gel pens are so smooth! Sometimes paying more for quality is worth it.

choices.label: 1 fancy refillable pen — $4.00
choices.effect: One great pen you can refill! Costs more upfront but less over time.

events.description: Shopping done! Let's look at your total spending and what you got. Was there a way to get even better value?

choices.label: I'm happy with my choices!
choices.effect: You made thoughtful decisions at every step! That's what smart shopping is about.

choices.label: I'd do some things differently next time
choices.effect: Reflecting on your choices helps you shop smarter next time! Great self-awareness.

choices.label: I saved money — let's see how much!
choices.effect: Let's count it up! Every dollar saved is a dollar you can use for something else.

recap_template: You practiced comparison shopping! You learned about unit prices, quality vs cost trade-offs, and making thoughtful purchasing decisions.
positive_framing_rules: Never say the student wasted money or bought the wrong thing
Frame both budget and quality choices as valid strategies
Celebrate the thinking process, not just the outcome
ai_variation_allowed: Add coupons or sales as surprises

title: Club Treasurer
learning_objectives: Manage a shared budget across multiple events
Track spending and communicate about money

events.description: You're the Science Club treasurer with $500 for the semester. The club wants 3 events: a field trip ($200), a science fair booth ($150), and an end-of-year pizza party ($100). That's $450 — but what about supplies for weekly meetings? Those cost about $10/week for 10 weeks ($100). The math doesn't add up! What's your plan?

choices.label: Cheaper field trip ($150) to cover supplies
choices.effect: A closer field trip saves $50! Now everything fits in the budget.

choices.label: Fundraise $100 for supplies separately
choices.effect: A candy sale raises $120! Supplies covered and $20 extra!

choices.label: Trim 10% from each event budget
choices.effect: Small cuts across the board save $45! Every category still gets most of its budget.

events.description: The science fair is coming up. Your $150 booth budget needs to cover materials ($80), a poster ($30), and prizes ($40). A club member found cheaper materials for $50. Do you keep the savings or upgrade something?

choices.label: Save the $30 as a buffer
choices.effect: A $30 buffer for unexpected costs. Treasurer thinking!

choices.label: Upgrade prizes to $70
choices.effect: Better prizes will attract more visitors! The booth will be a hit!

choices.label: Better poster ($45) and save $15
choices.effect: A more eye-catching poster plus a small buffer. Balanced upgrade!

events.description: Two members want to spend leftover money differently. One wants extra lab supplies, the other wants matching club t-shirts ($8 each for 20 people = $160). You only have $80 left.

choices.label: Lab supplies — serves the club's mission
choices.effect: Lab supplies help everyone learn! Aligned with the club's purpose.

choices.label: Find $4 shirts instead — $80 total!
choices.effect: Creative budgeting! Everyone gets a shirt at half the price!

choices.label: Put it to a club vote
choices.effect: The club votes and the decision feels fair to everyone!

events.description: End of semester! Time to present your financial report to the club advisor. How did you manage the $500?

choices.label: Show a detailed breakdown of all spending
choices.effect: Your clear report impresses the advisor! They see exactly where every dollar went.

choices.label: Highlight what you accomplished within budget
choices.effect: Three events, weekly supplies, and money saved! The advisor is proud of your work.

choices.label: Present a plan for next semester too
choices.effect: Forward thinking! The advisor loves that you're already planning ahead.

recap_template: You managed a club budget for a whole semester! You balanced competing needs, handled surprises, and made fair decisions. Real-world treasurer skills!
positive_framing_rules: Never say the student mismanaged money
Frame budget constraints as creative challenges
Celebrate communication and fairness in budget decisions
ai_variation_allowed: Vary the specific events and costs

title: Savings Goal Tracker
learning_objectives: Set and track a long-term savings goal

events.description: You want a $200 gaming headset and earn $25/week from chores. If you save everything, you'd have it in 8 weeks. But life happens! Week 1: your friend invites you to the movies ($15). Do you go?

choices.label: Skip the movie, save $25
choices.effect: Full $25 saved! You're 12.5% of the way there already!

choices.label: Go to the movie, save $10
choices.effect: Fun movie with your friend! $10 saved this week. Experiences matter too!

choices.label: Suggest a free hangout instead
choices.effect: Park hangout with your friend — just as fun AND you saved $25!

events.description: Week 4 check-in! You've saved some money but you're behind your $100 target. A neighbor offers you a one-time $30 job raking leaves. What do you do?

choices.label: Take the leaf-raking job
choices.effect: Extra $30! You're back on track or even ahead!

choices.label: Ask if they have more jobs next week too
choices.effect: They say yes! $30 this week and $20 next week. Entrepreneurial thinking!

choices.label: You're already on track, skip it
choices.effect: You checked your savings and you're doing fine! No need for extra work right now.

events.description: Week 6! The headset just went on sale for $170 — 15% off! But the sale ends this week and you have $155. What do you do?

choices.label: Keep saving — you'll have $200 in 2 weeks
choices.effect: Patience! In 2 weeks you'll have the full $200 and money to spare.

choices.label: Ask parents for a $15 advance on next week's chores
choices.effect: Parents agree! You get the sale price and pay it back next week. Smart negotiating!

choices.label: Look for a similar headset within your budget
choices.effect: You find a great option for $150! Under budget and highly rated!

events.description: Goal complete! You got your headset. Let's reflect on the journey.

choices.label: I learned that saving takes patience
choices.effect: Patience is a superpower! You proved you can work toward a big goal over time.

choices.label: I learned to be flexible with my plan
choices.effect: Adapting to changes made you a better saver! Plans can shift and that's okay.

choices.label: I learned I can earn more when I need to
choices.effect: Finding extra income showed real initiative! You took control of your goal.

recap_template: You saved for a $200 goal over 8 weeks! You handled temptations, found extra income, and adapted when prices changed. Long-term saving is a powerful skill.
positive_framing_rules: Never say the student spent carelessly or fell behind
Frame spending on experiences as valid alongside saving
